To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fabrication of self-organized waveguiding nano-structures can only be achieved by the epitaxial deposition of rod-like molecules on highly symmetric surfaces.
the molecular adsorption and the contact plane of the grown nano-fibres is a key parameter for the realization of self-assembled opto-electronic nano-structures.
the epitaxial fabrication of organic nano-structures can only be achieved by a precise control on molecular adsorption and crystal contact plane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel class of opto-electronics based on self-assembling organic nano-structures and the implementation of these nano-structures within opto-electric devices.
the fabrication and characterization of self-assembled optically active nano-structures.
the epitaxial fabrication and characterization of organic nano-fibres which are potentially useful for the fabrication of organic waveguiding structures and optical resonators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented growth concept is a fundamental and powerful strategy to control the fabrication of self-organized organic nano-structures and to expand the possible scope of molecular building blocks.
the fabrication of opto-active self-assembled nano-structures is a challenging and promising research field.

the fabrication of opto- and/or electro-active organic nano-structures is possible and the reported results demonstrate that this fabrication can be achieved by the utilization of a common valid concept.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epitaxially grown organic nano-structures can serve as a platform to develop novel opto-electronic nano-devices.
the presented growth model can be used to predict the molecular building block spectrum which is suitable for the fabrication of opto- electronic devices based on self- assembled organic nano-fibres.
the fabrication of opto-mechanical resonator structures based on epitaxially grown organic nano-fibres can be considered as an effective approach to fabricate nano-optical devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fabrication of self-organized nano-fibre based devices can be controlled by a combination of molecular adsorption geometry, substrate surface symmetry, crystal structure and the crystal contact-plane.
the epitaxial fabrication of self-assembling organic nano-structures can lead to a precise control on their orientation.
a precise control over the crystal growth parameters is the key for a successful fabrication of self-assembling organic opto-electronic nano-structures and devices.
